title: 1966 AHSME Problem 27
statement: At his usual rate a man rows \(15\) miles downstream in five hours less time than it takes him to return. If he doubles his usual rate, the time downstream is only one hour less than the time upstream. In miles per hour, the rate of the stream’s current is:

solutions.text:
The two time differences give \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{15}{v-c}-\frac{15}{v+c}&=5,\\ \frac{15}{2v-c}-\frac{15}{2v+c}&=1. \end{aligned} \] These simplify to \(v^2-c^2=6c\) and \(4v^2-c^2=30c.\) Substituting \(v^2=c^2+6c\) into the second gives \(3c^2-6c=0.\) Since \(c\gt0,\) we have \(c=2.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let \(v\) be the rower’s still-water speed and \(c\) the current speed
Translate the two time differences using speeds \(v\pm c\) and \(2v\pm c\)
